directories.doc:
Provide tagged application errors and Markdown compilation shared by server
operations, remotes, and components. Storage and request orchestration belong to
their owning directories.

Provide reusable Svelte presentation, form, dialog, and pagination components.
Consumers supply projections and callbacks; persistence and authorization belong
to callers.

Define shared business records, projections, aggregates, and pure functions used
by client and server modules. Group related data by business concept.

Models neither obtain external capabilities nor perform observable effects. They
must not import server infrastructure, SvelteKit request APIs, or component
code. Repository-specific SQL, transaction mechanisms, and operation parameters
stay in repositories; use-case dependency/parameter/result types stay beside
their operation. Page-only `ArticleDetail` and `CommentView` belong beside their
remote functions. Cookie transport data and cookie writers belong to the server
request-boundary helper. Invitation quota calculation belongs directly in the
relevant use case.

Imports have no observable effects.

Provide runtime composition and request-boundary authentication support. The
registry initializes the database and provider adapters; request helpers manage
cookies, OAuth request data, post-sign-in redirect targets, and locals. Business
operations live in use cases and do not import the registry or request helpers.

Provide request-independent GitHub OAuth, DNS TXT lookup, clock, and random
value generation capabilities. Request parsing, OAuth state-cookie validation,
and session cookies belong to `src/lib/server/auth.ts`; account and session
decisions belong to use cases. Adapters do not import SvelteKit request/cookie
types.

Own PostgreSQL connection construction, schema declarations, inferred storage
row types, and the generated SQL schema used by local database tooling.
Consumers are repositories, the server composition boundary, and database
management scripts. Business workflows and repository composition belong to
their owning modules.

Provide database reads, writes, model mapping, and internal transactions for
articles, bookmarks, comments, invitations, roles, sessions, and users.
Consumers pass `AppDatabase` from `src/lib/server/db/schema.ts` directly to
standalone exported functions.

Before changing or reviewing repository operations, apply the
[repository conventions](../architecture.md#repositories) for function
structure, data shapes, naming, errors, and transactions. Export
operation-specific object parameter types as `XxxParams` beside their function;
shared model values may also serve directly as inputs.

Use cases own permissions, business decisions, quota calculation, and session
lifetime policy. This module owns generated storage identifiers and persistence
timestamps; request context, cookies, DNS, and frontend state belong to callers.
Imports perform no queries.

Paginated results follow the [models contract](src=lib=models.md#paginated),
including requested page values and empty `items`. Related result/count queries
use a consistent snapshot, including paginated lists and invite statistics.
Preserve table constraints and identifier formats.

Provide isolated PostgreSQL databases for repository integration tests. Reuse
the checkout-local provisioning lifecycle; test cases exercise real SQL and
internal transactions without connecting to the development database.
Application code must not import this test-only module. Importing it performs no
I/O.

Implement server business operations that require external capabilities. Callers
supply capabilities in `deps` and invocation data in `params`; use cases import
repository functions and pass `deps.db`. Repositories own transactions and
persistence consistency. Request boundaries own request context, cookies,
redirects, and remote-query refreshes. Use cases neither import the service
registry nor read environment variables.

Deterministic Markdown compilation and business calculations stay in their
owning operations; only actual shared business scenarios receive separate
exported functions.

`AppDatabase` comes from `src/lib/server/db/schema.ts`; business data comes from
`src/lib/models`. Callers supply trusted authenticated actors, provider
identities, parsed URLs, and request-independent input values.
Repository/adapter failures propagate; expected business failures use tagged
application errors, with field keys for correctable input failures. Each use
case declares only the dependencies it uses. Request entry points supply `now`
from `adapters/clock.ts`; use cases never obtain the current time directly.

Provide the deterministic shared dataset used by local provisioning and browser
journeys, including relationships and derived interaction counts. Schema-derived
seed types import `src/lib/server/db/schema.ts`; shared roles and path helpers
import `src/lib/models`.

files.doc:
Request adaptation shared by hooks, remote functions, and route handlers. Models and use cases must not import
this module. Importing it performs no database, network, or cookie operation.

Table builders and their inferred row types; row and insert shapes come from each table's $inferSelect and
$inferInsert. Every table's createdAt and updatedAt are required and default to now. Tables declare no foreign
keys.

Read article models and projections; insert and update persisted articles together with their direct parent's
reply count.
Read bookmark state and keep relationship changes consistent with the article's persisted bookmark count.

Read comment records and per-user grouped projections; insert and update comments while preserving article
counts.
Persist invitation codes and expose consistent quota inputs. Quota arithmetic belongs to the invitation use case.
Read assigned roles and invitation relationships, and persist invitation redemption atomically.

Persist supplied session data. Use cases own ID generation, current-time reads, expiration decisions, and
renewal policy.
Read user identity and profile data, and persist supplied profile changes.

Operation wrapping and storage identifier generation shared by the repositories in this directory. These helpers
are not database operations themselves.
Create, validate, and invalidate the sessions behind the `auth_session` cookie.

Importing builds the shared dataset in memory once, with deterministic minute-spaced timestamps starting at
2026-01-01 UTC. No database or network work happens on import.
